title: Policy Shadowbox Drift — Incident Notes and Immediate Runbook
content:
Summary:
We saw a multi-tenant drift between the policy catalog (the authoritative ledger written by the control plane) and the on-prem firewall policy store for a subset of customers using Private/VPC deployments. Symptoms were intermittent packet drops and control-plane-reached-but-policy-mismatch errors surfaced by agent heartbeats. The reconcilers on hosts were replaying ledger deltas out of order for affected tenants leading to a temporary policy shadow (the agent reported a policy hash that did not match the catalog).

Impact:
- Affected customers: 3 tenants (two in EMEA, one in us-west) with on-prem firewalls in hybrid mode.
- User-visible: intermittent connection failures for services behind customer firewalls, lasted ~2h for the worst tenant, 5–10% increased p99 latency for control-plane sync endpoints.
- No data plane exfiltration observed. No customer data integrity loss.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-05-21T02:03 — First alert triggered: reconciler-error spike observed by metrics (reconcile_failures per-tenant) and alert INC-5892 created automatically.
- 2026-05-21T02:08 — SRE oncall (Hannah) acknowledged, opened pagerduty.
- 2026-05-21T02:15 — CS reported customer slack thread: "firewall blocking internal service calls intermittently".
- 2026-05-21T02:22 — Initial triage: observed policy hash mismatch between control-plane ledger and agent-applied hash for tenant acme-corp (hash: a3f4 vs expected a9b2).
- 2026-05-21T02:40 — Investigated reconciler logs: found repeated replays of the same delta id but with different sequencing; logs show leader election and a short window where the reconciler restarted and replay ordering was non-deterministic.
- 2026-05-21T03:05 — Mitigation: forced a full reconciler snapshot push for affected tenants and rolled forward agent-applier to perform a cold apply.
- 2026-05-21T04:30 — Metrics returned to baseline, customers reported restoration of connectivity.
- 2026-05-21T06:10 — Post-mitigation monitoring period ended; follow-ups scheduled.

Root cause hypotheses (initial):
1) Reconciler replay ordering race during leader election: when the control-plane leader moved, the new leader replayed recent deltas while the old leader replayed the same range, causing duplicated/different sequence numbers in the agent's view. The agent's sampler uses simple last-write ordering which is not idempotent across duplicate deltas.
2) Agent-side dedupe window too small: the agent uses a 30s dedupe cache keyed only by delta id; if the same delta arrives with different sequence metadata within that window it can be applied in the wrong position.
3) Network flaps triggered partial apply: intermittent connectivity during replay caused partial policy application sequences to persist on the firewall (rule half-applies).

Evidence collected (logs/metrics):
- reconciler logs (control-plane): repeated WARN entries 'replay: delta_seq_mismatch tenant=acme-corp delta=8421' with timestamps clustered around leader ejection.
- agent logs (applier): 'applier: applied rule-set v=8421 partial=true' followed by 'applier: apply_failed position=7/48' for some customers.
- telemetry: policy_hash_export shows two distinct hashes for same tenant across control-plane replicas during window.
- tcpdump from customer-provided box (redacted) shows TCP resets aligned with the time of partial applies.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Triggered forced full snapshot push (control-plane tool: /opt/control/bin/push_snapshot --tenant acme-corp) and validated checksums against agent-reported checksum after push.
- Restarted agent-applier on affected hosts (kubectl -n tenant-acme exec applier-*-pod -- supervisorctl restart applier).
- Applied emergency applied-state lock to prevent concurrent replays during leader transitions (soft lock implemented via feature flag).
- Communicated to CS and affected customers with status updates and ETA for full root cause fix.

Short-term fixes (next 72h):
- Increase agent dedupe window to 5m for delta ids and include sequence topology metadata in the dedupe key (owner: Diego).
- Add a pre-apply verification step: checksum verify the full rule-set before committing to firewall (owner: Lena).
- Enable stricter reconciliation backoff during leader transitions: when leader flaps detected, block replays for 60s and prefer snapshot push (owner: Ravi).

Long-term actions (postmortem/engineering):
- Reconciler redesign: ensure deltas are applied with a monotonic global sequence vector rather than local leader-assigned sequence numbers. This requires adding a small consensus marker to deltas (RFC to be written, owner: product/reconciler).
- Improved observability: per-tenant applied-vs-authoritative hash drift alert with automatic snapshot trigger when drift > 1 (owner: observability team).
- Agent transactional apply: change applier to perform atomic replace of ruleset rather than incremental patching to avoid half-applies.
- Chaos testing: add leader-election and replay-ordering scenarios to the onprem integration test matrix.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we have a guarantee that all control-plane nodes always serialize delta ids uniquely? If no, we need to add global sequencing and update agent semantics.
- Can customers' firewall vendors cause partial apply behavior (some vendors return success before internal commit)? Need to catalog vendor behaviors across affected tenants.
- Was there any correlation between high reconciler CPU cycles on a node and the sequencing anomalies? (initial look: some nodes were under CPU pressure but not conclusively causative).

For the runbook (draft) — immediate steps for oncall when seeing similar alert:
1) Identify affected tenants via metric: reconcile_failures{tenant!~""} and policy_hash_drift{tenant!~""}.
2) Check control-plane leader status: /opt/control/bin/leader_status --json; if leader has changed in last 120s, prioritize snapshot push.
3) If policy_hash_drift > 0.5 (fraction of rules), trigger emergency snapshot push for tenant: /opt/control/bin/push_snapshot --tenant <T> && verify sum via /opt/control/bin/verify_snapshot --tenant <T>.
4) Restart applier on customer-facing agents in rolling fashion: kubectl -n tenant-<T> rollout restart ds/applier --selector=zone=<zone> (wait 30s between zones).
5) Escalate to SRE eng-private-deployments and notify CS; post short status to slack channel #sre-private-incidents and tag PagerDuty.
6) If snapshot push fails or agents still show mismatch after push, open a bridge and collect: reconciler logs, applier logs, tcpdumps, and vendor debug output.

Notes / snippets observed while debugging (for engineers):
- Quick log grep: kubectl -n control-plane logs reconciler-0 | grep "replay" | sed -n '1,200p'
- Manual checksum: /opt/control/bin/checksum-ruleset --file /tmp/snapshot-acme-20260521.json
- Agent-level verification on host: sudo /usr/local/bin/applierctl status --tenant acme-corp --json

Communications timeline:
- 02:30 — CS first update to customer: "We're investigating an issue impacting firewall policy updates for some private deployments. Mitigations in progress."
- 04:45 — Second update: "We have pushed a full policy snapshot and are monitoring — connectivity should be restored. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

Owner-assigned next steps (for postmortem):
- Ravi: write the incident postmortem doc (link to be added) and coordinate the reconciler RFC. Due: 2026-05-28.
- Diego: ship agent dedupe metadata change as emergency patch. Due: 2026-05-25.
- Lena: prototype transactional replace applier and run integration tests with vendor firewall images. Due: 2026-06-04.
- Observability: add drift alert dashboard and auto-snapshot trigger experiment. Due: 2026-06-11.

Appendix — quick evidence table (copied from scratch notes):
- metric reconcile_failures spike: 02:03–02:25 UTC (tenant acme-corp, delta throughput 120/s burst)
- reconciler WARN pattern: replay: delta_seq_mismatch (counts: 37 instances)
- agent applier partial flags: 14 occurrences across 3 tenants
- tcpdump resets: 8 TCP RST in 10s window during partial apply

This is a working doc — please add notes inline. If you touched the control-plane or pushed any snapshots, add a short log note at the bottom with timestamp and username so we can reconstruct exact actions.

Recent edits log (manual):
- 2026-05-21T06:00 Ravi Menon: forced snapshot push for acme-corp and recorded verification checksums in linked artifact (JIRA INC-5892).
- 2026-05-21T06:13 Hannah Park: restarted applier pods in eu-west-1 cluster and observed applied hash converge.
- 2026-05-21T07:01 Diego Martinez: enabled emergency feature flag (replay-lock) for control-plane onprem mode.

End of notes.
